f3d4a2e3-eb53-49e7-a5da-ec8652734deb.content:
This was a simple one-time purchase of DOCN held from 2023-09-01 to 2026-09-09. The $1000 starting investment ended at $4962.59, a 396.26 percent gain. The result was driven by a very strong rise in DigitalOcean's share price, not by adding money or trading in and out. The test shows 1 executed fill.

DigitalOcean is a smaller cloud-computing company that provides online infrastructure and tools for developers and growing businesses. During this period, investors increasingly focused on whether it could benefit from demand for artificial intelligence computing, while still growing its regular cloud business.

The company reported improving business results during 2024. In its February 2025 results announcement, DigitalOcean said fourth-quarter revenue rose 13 percent from a year earlier, while revenue from its largest customers grew much faster. It also said AI-related products were gaining traction, and reported stronger profits and cash generation. These facts help explain why investors became more interested in the company. The connection to the share-price gain is an inference, not proof that any single announcement caused the entire return.

Holding it was far from comfortable. The test's worst fall began on 2025-02-18, when the portfolio was worth $1747.10, and ended on 2025-08-01 at $963.34. That was a 44.86 percent drop from a previous high. In practical terms, the investment temporarily fell below its original $1000 value before recovering. This is the main lesson of the test: the large final gain came with a long and severe period of loss along the way.

The timing also fits the news. DigitalOcean's February 2025 results were released during the decline, so good company numbers did not immediately prevent the shares from falling. That suggests investors were judging the stock on more than current results, including expectations about future growth, competition, and how much of the AI opportunity was already reflected in the price. That explanation is an interpretation of the price path and the company reporting, rather than a fact established by the backtest alone.

The recovery became much more visible after the company's second-quarter 2025 report. SiliconANGLE reported that revenue rose 14 percent year over year, AI offerings were seeing strong adoption, and DigitalOcean raised its full-year revenue outlook. The report also said the shares jumped nearly 29 percent that day. This provides a plausible explanation for the rebound after the August 1 low: investors received evidence that growth and AI demand were stronger than expected. It does not explain every later move through 2026.

Compared with SPY, which represents a broad basket of large US companies, DOCN was dramatically more rewarding in this particular test. SPY returned 68.98 percent, while DOCN returned 396.26 percent, a difference of 327.27 percentage points. The broad market also benefited from enthusiasm around technology and AI, and from a strong recovery after market concerns in 2025. But DOCN's result was much more concentrated. A single company with a narrower business can rise far more than the market when its story improves, and can also suffer much larger setbacks when confidence weakens.

So the plain-English summary is: DigitalOcean went from a promising but volatile smaller cloud company to a market favorite as its growth, profitability, and AI business appeared to improve. The holder was rewarded eventually, but had to sit through a nearly half-sized loss first. The final result beat the broad market by a wide margin, while offering a much rougher ride.

763a5d41-a4f7-4e17-9ac6-ef247f5b559b.content:
This historical DOCN run had a strong outcome, but the ride was demanding: the portfolio climbed sharply, then gave back a substantial portion of its high before finishing well above the money contributed. Holding through it meant accepting a 42.1% flow-adjusted drawdown, shown here only as a $421.20 illustration against the $1,000 starting capital, not as the actual peak-to-trough dollar loss.

Against the same monthly funding plan in SPY, DOCN came out ahead by 176.8 percentage points over this test window. The tradeoff was concentration and volatility: the result was much stronger historically, but with a bumpier path. A useful next question is whether the same monthly contribution plan produces a similar balance between return and drawdown over a different historical window.

result_readout_content.text:
This historical DOCN run had a strong outcome, but the ride was demanding: the portfolio climbed sharply, then gave back a substantial portion of its high before finishing well above the money contributed. Holding through it meant accepting a 42.1% flow-adjusted drawdown, shown here only as a $421.20 illustration against the $1,000 starting capital, not as the actual peak-to-trough dollar loss.

Against the same monthly funding plan in SPY, DOCN came out ahead by 176.8 percentage points over this test window. The tradeoff was concentration and volatility: the result was much stronger historically, but with a bumpier path. A useful next question is whether the same monthly contribution plan produces a similar balance between return and drawdown over a different historical window.
